a.title: Build pi's base system prompt sections (preamble, tools, rules, cwd)
a.body:
Follow-up to #51 ([comparison](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/issues/51#issuecomment-6863264436)). pi 1.5.2 builds its system prompt in `buildSystemPromptSections` (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/system-prompt.js`). pi-action sends **no** base prompt: the system message's `content` is `""`, and the model gets only `project_context`, `available_skills`, and the extensions' sections. The model is never told what it is, which tools it has, pi's general rules, or **its working directory**.

## What pi sends (project `xyz`, default tools)

The sections, in order (each tagged `<name>…</name>`, except `preamble`):

1. `preamble`: `You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.`
2. `tools`: one line per **declared** tool that has a prompt snippet, then `Additional tools may be available.` Example:
   ```
   - read: Read file contents
   - bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
   - edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
   - write: Create or overwrite files
   ```
   With no declared tools that have snippets: `(none)`.
3. `rules`: `buildRules()`, with duplicates removed:
   - With bash and without grep, find, or ls: `Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find`
   - The guidelines of each declared tool (read: `Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.`; edit: two lines; write: `Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.`). Leave out bash's `PI_*` environment-variable line: pi-action doesn't set those variables.
   - `Be concise in your responses`, `Show file paths clearly when working with files`
4. `docs`: pi's documentation paths. **Leave this out**: pi-action ships no pi docs.
5. `addendum`: APPEND_SYSTEM.md (separate issue).
6. `project_context`, then `skills`: pi-action has these already.
7. `cwd`: `/home/runner/work/xyz/xyz`
8. Extension sections (pit's).

## Proposal

Add these sections to the built-in `pi-action` extension (`src/builtin-extension.ts`):

- **Order.** pi-durable renders sections in install order (`CodingTools`, `pi-action-context`, `pi-action`, then the extensions). For pi's order (preamble, tools, rules before `project_context`, and `cwd` after `skills`), either split the sections across extensions, or move `project_context` into the built-in extension so that one extension owns pi's whole ordered list. The second is simpler. Keep the extensions' wraps working (`wrapSection("project_context" | "available_skills" | …)`), and document the new keys in `docs/extensions.md`.
- **Untagged preamble.** Use `tag: false` for `preamble`, as pi does.
- **Tool lines and rules come from the request.** Render them from `input.agent.tools` (the tools offered, after `exclude_tools`, `model_tools_hidden`, and the wraps), so they always match the tools declared to the model. For example, in a pit-only setup (#58) the model sees only `typescript`. Snippets and guidelines: pi-durable's `ToolRegistration` has no `promptSnippet` or `promptGuidelines`. Keep a table for `read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash` with pi's text (copied from pi-coding-agent 1.5.2, with a test that pins the version), and let a tool declare its own. pit already exports `PROMPT_SNIPPET`, and puts its guidelines in `pit_guidelines`, so don't repeat them in `rules`.
- **Same text every request.** Each section renders the same text for the whole run (the tool set is fixed per run), so the prompt cache holds.
- **Existing threads** get the sections as a positional system update on their next request. Check that `planSystemEntries` doesn't reorder the sections the thread already shows, or accept the one remove-and-re-add.
- **No `prompt_template` change.** It shapes only the first user message.

## Tests and docs

- Tests:
  - The section text for the default tools, pit-only tools, `exclude_tools: bash`, and no tools.
  - The order of the whole rendered system prompt.
  - Unchanged across two requests in one run.
- Docs:
  - `docs/prompts.md`: a new "The system prompt" part listing every section in order.
  - `docs/how-it-works.md`, `docs/extensions.md` (section keys for wraps).

@pi please implement this and open a PR. Follow CONTRIBUTING.md, run `npm run check`, and update the docs.

b.title: Add a thinking_level input (default: pi's medium)
b.body:
Follow-up to #51 ([comparison](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/issues/51#issuecomment-6863264436)). pi picks a thinking level in this order: the model's scoped `thinkingLevel`, then the per-model setting, then `defaultThinkingLevel`, then `DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL = "medium"` (`pi-coding-agent/dist/core/defaults.js`, `model-resolver.js`). pi-action never sets one, so pi-durable's `resolveAgent` uses `state?.thinkingLevel ?? "off"`. Every run is **off**, even with `model_reasoning: true`. pi has no setting that matches this.

## Proposal

- **New input:** `thinking_level`, one of `off | minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh` (pi-ai's `ModelThinkingLevel`). Default `medium`.
- **Apply it on every run.** In `Thread.open`, add `thinkingLevel` to the `agent` that `configureAgent` passes to `root.configure`. A thread started under another level then switches on the next run, as the model does.
- **Models without reasoning.** When the model has no reasoning support (built-in model metadata, or `model_reasoning: false` for a custom model), send `off`, and write a log line instead of failing. pi does the same: it caps the level to what the model supports. Check how pi-ai maps levels for each provider (`thinkingLevelMap`, `compat_force_adaptive_thinking`, `supportsReasoningEffort`), and add a test with the faux provider that the level reaches the request options.
- **Release notes.** Mention it: the default moves runs from off to medium, so they may cost more tokens. This is a `feat` that matches pi. Set `thinking_level: off` to keep the old behavior.
- **Setup log.** Show the level in the `🤖` line (`🤖 anthropic/claude-… · thinking medium · …`).

## Tests and docs

- Tests:
  - Parsing the input, rejecting invalid values.
  - The configured `thinkingLevel` and the downgrade to `off` for models without reasoning.
  - A changed level on a continuing thread.
- Docs:
  - README inputs table, `docs/models.md` (a "Thinking" section), `action.yml`.

@pi please implement this and open a PR. Follow CONTRIBUTING.md, run `npm run check`, and update the docs.

c.title: Support SYSTEM.md and APPEND_SYSTEM.md
c.body:
Follow-up to #51 ([comparison](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/issues/51#issuecomment-6863264436)). pi lets a project or user replace or extend its system prompt (`resource-loader.js`, `discoverSystemPromptFile` / `discoverAppendSystemPromptFile`):

| File | Effect in pi | Lookup |
|---|---|---|
| `SYSTEM.md` | Replaces pi's own sections (preamble, tools, rules, docs) as `customPrompt`. `project_context`, `skills`, `cwd`, and extension sections still follow | `<cwd>/.pi/SYSTEM.md` **if the project is trusted**, else `<agent dir>/SYSTEM.md` |
| `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` | Added as the `addendum` section, after the base sections | `<cwd>/.pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md` if trusted, else `<agent dir>/APPEND_SYSTEM.md` |

pi-action reads neither file.

## Proposal (depends on the base-prompt issue)

- **Lookup.** The same as pi's. Project files only with `trust_project: true`, because anyone who can push a branch can change them. User files from `<agent_dir>/`, only when the `agent_dir` input is set.
- **SYSTEM.md** replaces the `preamble`, `tools`, and `rules` sections from the base-prompt issue with one untagged `preamble` that holds the file's text. The other sections stay.
- **APPEND_SYSTEM.md** becomes an `addendum` section between `rules` and `project_context`.
- **Fork pull requests.** As for `AGENTS.md` (#53): read project files from the base commit, or skip them. Since they need `trust_project` anyway, skipping on forks with a log line is simplest.
- **Read once per run.** Remove the BOM and invisible characters, as `context-files.ts` does. Count the files toward `context_files_max_bytes`, or give them their own limit.
- **Setup log:** `System prompt: .pi/SYSTEM.md (replaces pi's base prompt)`, `Appended: agent_dir/APPEND_SYSTEM.md`, or a line saying why a project file was skipped (not trusted, fork).
- **Input.** Consider an input that turns this off, or reuse `context_files: false`. pi uses one switch for context files only, so a separate `system_prompt_files` input (default `true`) is clearer.

## Tests and docs

- Tests:
  - Lookup order: trusted project, then user.
  - Untrusted and fork skipping.
  - SYSTEM.md replaces only the base sections.
  - APPEND_SYSTEM.md position.
  - Unchanged within a run.
- Docs:
  - `docs/prompts.md` (system prompt), `docs/security.md` (project files), README inputs.

@pi please implement this and open a PR once the base-prompt issue is merged (or together with it). Follow CONTRIBUTING.md, run `npm run check`, and update the docs.

d.title: Match pi's context file names and <project_instructions> layout
d.body:
Follow-up to #51 ([comparison](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/issues/51#issuecomment-6863264436)) and #53. pi-action's `project_context` section differs from pi 1.5.2 in two ways.

## 1. File names

pi's `loadContextFileFromDir` (`pi-coding-agent/dist/core/resource-loader.js`) takes the first file that exists, in this order:

```
AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.md, AGENTS.MD, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.MD
```

pi-action's `CONTEXT_FILE_NAMES` (`src/context-files.ts`) has only `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. Use pi's list, in pi's order, everywhere it's used:

- The global `agent_dir` file.
- Each directory from the workspace root to `cwd`.
- The nested-file listing.
- Fork pull requests, where `git ls-tree` and `git show` read from the base commit: the matches are case-sensitive, so `AGENTS.MD` must be its own entry.

Skip directories named like these files (pi checks `isFile()`).

## 2. Layout

pi renders:

```
<project_context>
Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

<project_instructions path="/home/runner/work/xyz/xyz/AGENTS.md">
…content…
</project_instructions>

<project_instructions path="/home/runner/work/xyz/xyz/packages/api/AGENTS.md">
…
</project_instructions>
</project_context>
```

pi-action renders the older `# Project Context` / `## <path>` layout. Use pi's layout, as `renderProjectContext()` does. Keep pi-action's additions after the files, as plain lines inside `project_context`:

- The nested-file note.
- The size-limit note.
- The fork base-commit note.

Keep the content trimmed, as pi does (pi removes the BOM; pi-action also removes invisible characters, which is fine).

Existing threads get one `Updated system prompt section "project_context"` on their next run. That's acceptable.

## Tests and docs

- Tests:
  - Each name in the precedence order, with two names present in one directory.
  - A directory named `AGENTS.md`.
  - Fork base-commit lookup with `AGENTS.override.md`.
  - The exact section text.
- Docs:
  - `docs/prompts.md` / `docs/how-it-works.md` (file names, layout), and the README if it names the files.

@pi please implement this and open a PR. Follow CONTRIBUTING.md, run `npm run check`, and update the docs.
